summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a chronic suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent drug-resistant urinary tract infections, was admitted for confusion and fever. He was found to have sepsis due to Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteremia originating from an obstructing left ureteral stone causing hydronephrosis. He underwent urgent placement of a left percutaneous nephrostomy for drainage and was started on IV antibiotics. Blood cultures cleared, and he transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin. His condition improved with normalized kidney function and resolution of infection. He was discharged home with instructions to complete a 14-day antibiotic course, restart suppressive fosfomycin therapy, follow up with urology for surgical evaluation of stone burden, and schedule pulmonary function testing prior to any procedure.
